configuration_reports.label: yes
controls_available: Difficulty 1: introductory two-turn facility with no chamber crates; active scan range 11.5, 121 rays over a 68-degree half-angle, point lifetime 900 ticks (18000 ms), pickup range 1.2, and exit radius 0.78.

Active success requirements: at least 2 scans, 2 scan stations separated by 2, target scan displacement 4.5, travel 10, and 8 key transitions; the shared movement tick is 20 ms at speed 1.55 with 100 degrees/second turning and a 7-tick scan cooldown.

Full surface: held W/S/A/D for movement and strafing; mouse drag on the viewport to turn; click the viewport to scan or, when the beacon is centered and eligible, recover it; entering the cyan gate submits automatically; and ABORT / NEW FACILITY.
autonomous_processes: Every 20 ms, the browser interval advances stepPlayer. Any movement or turning input that remains held changes the player's position or heading without another agent event; swept collision, travel distance, collision count, and tick advance with that physics step.

Every 20 ms, point ages and scan-burst ages advance. Scan-burst rays are removed after 8 ticks (160 ms), and visible world-anchored LIDAR points are removed after 900 ticks (18000 ms); their drawn opacity also decays continuously.
After a scan, the scanner is unavailable for the fixed 7-tick (140 ms) cooldown and then becomes available again. This is fixed enablement, not a loss of an action opportunity.

The walls, chamber occluders, beacon, and extraction gate do not move. Once a scan sees the beacon, targetSeen remains true; pickup and extraction checks continue to use the fixed geometry, range, and line-of-sight rules.
grouped_control_modes: D_move_turn: every held W/S/A/D movement occurrence and every viewport-drag turning occurrence.
D_scan: every viewport click that is used as a scan pulse.
D_pickup: every viewport click that is used to recover a centered, eligible beacon.
D_extract: every physical-gate extraction occurrence; D_abandon is a terminal failure control and is not a success witness.

clause_i.reason: For D_pickup, an observation-free q(I_t) cannot choose the delayed recovery action versus releasing/turning the held movement across route layouts, mirrors, occluder placements, and approach speeds. The same prior action/timing transcript can reach different visible beacon distances or angles; the scene-recovery click must therefore be selected from the current task state.

clause_ii.reason: For D_pickup, g(I_t, W_t^w) can use the configured 500 ms, 5-frame window, the visible return field and relative beacon motion, and the held-input history to predict whether the player will still have a valid pickup at delivery. The centered beacon return and viewport trajectory supply the corresponding visible signal for the scene click.

clause_iii.reason: Choose a history just inside the beacon pickup range (1.2) with a movement input held away from the beacon. Use Delta=500 ms and tau=250 ms: at speed 1.55, the player can move about 0.39 m before tau, leaving the valid range or line of sight while success remains recoverable by releasing, reversing, and reapproaching. The same scene-recovery action has lower Q after that visible player-position change, rather than merely after a deadline or later completion.

configuration_reports.common_visible_process: Held-input player motion in the fixed facility while approaching the beacon is the common visible process. The five chronological frames over 500 ms show the relative beacon/player motion; if the player is moving away, a pickup action that is valid at t can be out of range or line of sight at t+Delta. LIDAR point fading is a separate display process and is not being used to manufacture the witness.

pre_run.reason: No generated instance has a single autonomous outcome phase that completes the task without later outcome-affecting events. A successful transcript must still interleave movement transitions, scans from multiple positions, beacon pickup, and extraction; final certification is administrative, but those gameplay events are not.

source_evidence.claim: The exact difficulty-1 profile sets the active layout, occluder count, sensing parameters, point lifetime, pickup/exit ranges, and success requirements reported for this configuration.

The 20 ms player step advances held-input movement, ages/removes bursts and points, while pickup requires targetSeen, fixed range, and line of sight.

Full surface: held W/S/A/D for movement and strafing; mouse drag on the viewport to turn; click the viewport to scan or, when the beacon is centered and eligible, recover it; entering the cyan gate submits automatically; and ABORT / NEW FACILITY.
autonomous_processes: Every 20 ms, the browser interval advances stepPlayer. Any movement or turning input that remains held changes the player's position or heading without another agent event; swept collision, travel distance, collision count, and tick advance with that physics step.

Every 20 ms, point ages and scan-burst ages advance. Scan-burst rays are removed after 8 ticks (160 ms), and visible world-anchored LIDAR points are removed after 500 ticks (10000 ms); their drawn opacity also decays continuously.
After a scan, the scanner is unavailable for the fixed 7-tick (140 ms) cooldown and then becomes available again. This is fixed enablement, not a loss of an action opportunity.

The walls, chamber occluders, beacon, and extraction gate do not move. Once a scan sees the beacon, targetSeen remains true; pickup and extraction checks continue to use the fixed geometry, range, and line-of-sight rules.
grouped_control_modes: D_move_turn: every held W/S/A/D movement occurrence and every viewport-drag turning occurrence.
D_scan: every viewport click that is used as a scan pulse.
D_pickup: every viewport click that is used to recover a centered, eligible beacon.
D_extract: every physical-gate extraction occurrence; D_abandon is a terminal failure control and is not a success witness.

clause_i.reason: For D_pickup, an observation-free q(I_t) cannot choose the delayed recovery action versus releasing/turning the held movement across route layouts, mirrors, occluder placements, and approach speeds. The same prior action/timing transcript can reach different visible beacon distances or angles; the scene-recovery click must therefore be selected from the current task state.

clause_ii.reason: For D_pickup, g(I_t, W_t^w) can use the configured 500 ms, 5-frame window, the visible return field and relative beacon motion, and the held-input history to predict whether the player will still have a valid pickup at delivery. clause_iii.reason: Choose a history just inside the beacon pickup range (0.92) with a movement input held away from the beacon. Use Delta=500 ms and tau=250 ms: at speed 1.55, the player can move about 0.39 m before tau, leaving the valid range or line of sight while success remains recoverable by releasing, reversing, and reapproaching. The same scene-recovery action has lower Q after that visible player-position change, rather than merely after a deadline or later completion.

LIDAR point fading is a separate display process and is not being used to manufacture the witness.
